blocks.text: Tuesday: Cotopaxi National Park and return to Quito

paragraphs.ref: text:Day 8 (Tuesday) · Cotopaxi National Park, created in 1975, covers about 33,000 hectares of volcanoes and lakes, home to condors, pumas, spectacled bears and Andean foxes. Visit the park museum, then walk 30 minutes to the Limpiopungo lagoon, which reflects Rumiñahui Volcano, a fine spot for birds. Return to Quito for a city tour: panoramic views, historic churches and beautifully decorated rooftops, with insights into the colonial art and architecture of the capital. Founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca city, at about 2,850 m, Quito survived several earthquakes and keeps one of the best-preserved historic centres in Latin America, with ornate interiors showcasing the Quito School of Art, a fusion of Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and Indigenous influences; it was among the very first places inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List. Overnight at Hotel Plaza Grande. (B, L)
